title: Chapter 107: Hidden Edge 1
content:
Chapter 107

Hidden Edge 1

Jin Guangyao gritted his teeth, his free fingers flying as he tapped several pressure points along his severed stump. The dizzying, hollow thrum of catastrophic blood loss hit him all at once, making the room tilt. Through the grey blur, his vision locked onto Nie Mingjue. The hulking corpse had just taken a heavy step toward him, milky, vacant eyes pinned straight onto his face.

Every drop of blood left in Jin Guangyao turned to ice.

Beside him, Su She hacked up another mouthful of gore, clutching his battered ribs as he shrieked at the top of his lungs, "You useless idiots! What the hell are you standing around for?! Block him! Don't let that thing past the doors!"

Snapping out of their dazed stupor, the surviving Lanling Jin cultivators drew their steel and swarmed forward. Before the vanguard could even plant their feet, Nie Mingjue’s massive palm caught the first two, sending them hurtling across the flagstones like ragdolls.

Jin Guangyao fumbled desperately, shaking white medicinal powder over the bloody stump with his left hand, but the crimson torrent was rushing so fast it washed the medicine away before it could take hold. Fighting back hot, frantic tears, he tried to rip a strip off his inner robes to tourniquet the wound. But his left arm had already been blistered raw by the toxic mist from the coffin; the fingers were dead weight, trembling so violently that every tug merely ground agonizing blisters against his skin without tearing so much as a thread.

Scrambling across the wet floor on hands and knees, Su She threw himself at Jin Guangyao’s side, tearing clean strips from his own white robes to bind the limb. Nearby, Lan Xichen was shielding Nie Huaisang as they retreated toward a dry pocket of the hall.

Su She’s hands patted frenziedly around his own belt, finding nothing. In sheer desperation, he looked toward Lan Xichen, his voice cracking: "Lan-zongzhu! Lan-zongzhu, do you have any medicine?! Please, lend a hand! Our sect leader has treated you with nothing but pristine courtesy this entire time—for the love of heaven, show some mercy!"

Taking in Jin Guangyao’s chalk-white, half-dead state, Lan Xichen’s eyes flickered with a raw wave of reluctant pity.

Before he could answer, another chorus of bone-chilling shrieks shredded the air. Nie Mingjue drove a bare fist into the fray, pulping three cultivators into a gruesome spray of scarlet paste in a single strike.

Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji held the line, keeping their backs firmly braced in front of Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling.

"Wen Ning!" Wei Wuxian called out, eyes never leaving the doorway. "Where the hell did you run into him?!"

Wen Ning, having just casually popped his dislocated wrist back into its socket, was busy wrenching his bent kneecap back into place. "You told me to fetch Young Master Lan, but I couldn't find him at the inn, so I had to scour the main streets. Before I crossed paths with him, I spotted Chifeng-zun prowling through town, looking like he was hunting for a trail. A pack of street urchins saw him in the dark, and not realizing the danger, figured he was like me and started roughhousing around him. Chifeng-zun’s mind is completely gone; he moved to tear them in half with his bare hands. I had no choice but to trade blows with him all the way here..."

As for why Wen Ning hadn't found Lan Wangji in his room, Wei Wuxian didn't even need to ask. If Wei Wuxian had spent the night tossing and turning on the wrong side of the adjoining wall, was the pristine, upright Hanguang-jun supposed to sleep like a baby? The man had clearly wandered out into the streets to burn off the restless steam, bumping right into Fairy as the dog was racing off to fetch reinforcements.

And this sudden, apocalyptic deluge—it had definitely kicked up the second Wen Ning and Nie Mingjue crossed fists.

Fierce corpses were natural conduits for dark malice, gathering ominous energies wherever they walked. To have two apex calamities throwing hands in one place? It was practically daring the heavens to drop a tempest.

Though outclassed to a comical degree, the remaining Lanling Jin disciples kept charging in like moths to an open flame. Yet when their spiritual steel collided with Nie Mingjue’s frame, the blades rang out with dull, metallic clangs as though hitting solid reinforced iron—failing to carve out so much as a hairline scratch.

Peering out from behind Lan Xichen’s sleeve, Nie Huaisang looked caught between stark terror and a desperate glimmer of hope. "D-D-Da-ge... It's me, I'm—"

Nie Mingjue’s pupilless white eyes flared wide with wild, unchecked rage. His arm lashed out, clawing straight for his brother’s throat!

Lan Xichen tilted his head, bringing Liebing to his lips in a flash. A single, mournful cry tore from the jade flute, causing the hulking giant to freeze dead in his tracks.

"Da-ge, look!" Lan Xichen urged, voice thick with emotion. "It’s Huaisang!"

Nie Huaisang whimpered, his face crumbling. "He doesn't even know who I am..."

"He doesn't just not know you," Wei Wuxian cut in, voice grim. "He doesn't even know himself anymore!"

Nie Mingjue was running on pure, unadulterated resentful energy—a walking meat-grinder driven entirely by violent, indiscriminate slaughter.

Having reset his broken bones, Wen Ning threw himself back into the clash. But his own grudge couldn't hold a candle to Nie Mingjue’s suffocating malice, his stature was outmatched by half a head, and with Wei Wuxian’s bamboo flute snapped in two, there was no way to channel dark arrays to back him up. Wen Ning was steadily losing ground.

Over by the pillar, Jin Guangyao’s bleeding stump had finally been staunchly bound. Scrambling to his feet, Su She hoisted the half-conscious clan leader onto his back, desperate to slip out through the chaos.

The sudden movement instantly set off Nie Mingjue’s hair-trigger instincts.

With a brutal shove, the giant batted Wen Ning across the room, turning on his heel to stalk straight toward Jin Guangyao with thunderous strides.

Jin Ling lost his head completely, screaming out on pure reflex: "Little Uncle! Run!"

Seeing the boy actively warning the enemy, Jiang Cheng’s hand came down hard against the back of Jin Ling’s skull. "Shut your mouth!" he barked.

The stinging slap dragged Jin Ling’s wits back into his skull. But this was the man who had doted on him for over a decade; watching his uncle about to be ground into paste under a feral corpse had torn the warning right out of his throat before his brain could catch up.

Yet the shout had already done its damage. Nie Mingjue paused, his head tilting toward the boy with a flicker of dull, primal curiosity.

Wei Wuxian’s gut dropped through the floorboards. Shit!

As a mindless fierce corpse, Nie Mingjue's deepest, most burning vendetta was naturally with his murderer, Jin Guangyao. But monsters like him didn't hunt using their eyes!

Jin Guangyao and Jin Ling shared thick, direct bloodlines. To an entity woven from pure malice and death, the scent, pulse, and living qi of these two warm-blooded bodies were nearly indistinguishable. When a creature’s mind was reduced to muddy static, telling them apart was almost impossible.

Right now, Jin Guangyao had lost an arm; his life force was running paper-thin, bleeding out and smelling half-dead. Jin Ling, on the other hand, was practically radiating pure, untouched vitality. To the hollow, unthinking instincts of a dead predator, the boy was an infinitely more tempting target.

Lan Wangji whipped Bichen forward, aiming straight for the center of the giant's chest. Sure enough, the crystalline tip slammed against the meat and stopped dead, held back by rock-hard muscle.

Glancing down at the glittering blade against his chest, Nie Mingjue let out a guttural, bone-shattering roar, clawing outward to shatter the steel. Lan Wangji recalled the sword on a razor's edge, Bichen snapping back into its scabbard with a sharp, resonant chime. In the same breath, Lan Wangji's left wrist flicked outward, manifesting the seven-stringed Wangji guqin flat across his forearm.

Without missing a beat, his fingertips tore across the silk strings, sending an icy, crystalline melody ringing through the hall.

Lan Xichen brought Liebing back to his mouth, joining the song.

Wei Wuxian dug into his sleeve, hurling a fan of over fifty yellow talismans through the air in a single, sweeping arc. Yet before the paper could even kiss Nie Mingjue's collar, the roiling black resentment radiating off the corpse ignited them midair, reducing the entire flurry to floating gray ash.

Bellowing in blind fury, Nie Mingjue lunged toward Jin Ling!

Backed straight into the temple corner, Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling had nowhere left to run. Jiang Cheng shoved the boy behind his own body, drawing Sandu with his right hand—despite his core running on absolute fumes—bracing himself to meet the blow with raw steel.

The guqin and xiao harmonized in a desperate crescendo, but it was too late.

Nie Mingjue’s iron fist drove forward, punching straight through a living chest.

Yet the body impaled on that fist belonged neither to Jiang Cheng nor Jin Ling.

Wen Ning stood wedged in the corner, planting himself squarely between the giant and the two heirs. Both of his gray hands clamped down on Nie Mingjue’s forged-iron arm, slowly, agonizingly wrenching the limb out from his own sternum. The impact left a massive, gaping cavern straight through his torso—no blood, only a rain of charred, desiccated black viscera tumbling onto the tiles.

"Wen Ning!" Wei Wuxian yelled.

Jiang Cheng looked like his brain had just short-circuited entirely, ready to lose his mind on the spot.

"You?!" Jiang Cheng gasped, choked with disbelief. "Why the hell did you—?!"

The raw kinetic force behind the strike hadn't just punched a hole through Wen Ning's chest; it had rattled his dead vocal cords to splinters. Incapable of producing a single syllable, the Ghost General’s knees buckled, his frame collapsing sideways.

He fell right across Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling's laps. His limbs were temporarily paralyzed from the shock, yet his glassy, unblinking eyes stayed locked onto their faces.

Jin Ling had spent his entire childhood harboring a bottomless, venomous hatred for this walking weapon—the very monster whose palm had punched a hole through his father's heart. He had sworn to the heavens countless times that if he ever got the chance, he would peel the flesh from Wei Ying and Wen Ning inch by bloody inch. Later, when he found himself unable to hate Wei Wuxian, that festering rage had doubled down, laser-focused entirely onto Wen Ning.

Yet right now, watching the murderer take the exact same fist through the heart to shield him... Jin Ling couldn't even bring himself to shove the corpse off his lap.

He knew Wen Ning was already dead. The guy could take a hole through his ribs or get cleaved in half at the waist and walk it off eventually. But watching that hollow chest, hot, helpless tears spilled over Jin Ling's lashes anyway.

Landing that punch had thrown Nie Mingjue’s momentum off for a split second.

Behind him, Lan Wangji and Lan Xichen played in seamless, relentless unison. The guqin flowed like an icy subterranean stream while the xiao cut through the air like a bitter winter wind. Every vibration was tuned precisely to the notes Nie Mingjue loathed most; the dissonant chord work ground against his dead meridians, wrapping him in an invisible, tightening net of spiritual tension.

Suffocated by the binding notes, Nie Mingjue’s rage spiked to an absolute boiling point. With a feral roar, he tore clean through the wards, swinging around to crush the guqin player where he stood.

Lan Wangji pivoted on his heel with immaculate grace, slipping past the lethal arc without missing a single, shimmering note.

Nie Mingjue’s fist blasted through the brick wall behind him, spitting a shower of powdered mortar.

Just as the giant moved to wrench his arm free and pivot, a crisp, jaunty whistle echoed through the hall.

Pulling his fist from the stone, Nie Mingjue turned his hollow gaze toward the sound.

Wei Wuxian loosed another pair of airy, trilling notes between his teeth, flashing a bright, easy grin. "Evening, Chifeng-zun. Care to remember an old friend?"

Nie Mingjue’s blank, milk-white eyeballs stared him down in unblinking silence.

Wei Wuxian chuckled softly. "Doesn't ring a bell? That's fine. As long as you remember the tune."

Lan Xichen lowered his xiao an inch, his voice tight: "Master Wei!"

He meant to warn him that the vessel he was wearing belonged to Mo Xuanyu—who was Jin Guangyao’s flesh and blood, a far closer relation than Jin Ling. If Nie Mingjue caught the scent of that lineage, all that bloodlust would snap straight onto his head.

Before the sect leader could finish the thought, Lan Wangji cast a fleeting, serene glance in his direction, giving a quiet, unshakable shake of his head.

Lan Xichen understood the look immediately: Stand down. Trust him.

Lan Wangji knew Wei Wuxian had this entirely in hand.

A bright, rolling whistle danced past Wei Wuxian's lips as he strolled forward with lazy, unhurried steps. The melody was jaunty and relaxed, yet ringing out beneath the storm, framed by lightning and rotting corpses, the bright tune carried an uncanny, hair-raising edge.

Down in the corner, Wen Ning seemed to catch the pull of the melody; a violent urge rippled through his paralyzed limbs, willing him to stand. He twitched twice, but his shattered core couldn't manage the leap, and he slumped sideways again. Both Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling reached out instinctively to keep the dead man from hitting the cold tiles—only to catch themselves simultaneously, freezing with near-identical, deeply conflicted grimaces, looking like they wanted to throw the corpse across the room and run.

Hands clasped casually behind his small of his back, Wei Wuxian kept up that teasing, mischievous tune as he took slow, rhythmic steps backward.

Nie Mingjue remained rooted to the spot.

One step back: the giant showed zero interest.

Three steps back: completely stone-faced.

By the seventh step, the primal tether embedded in the melody finally broke through the static. Nie Mingjue lifted a heavy boot, taking a lumbering stride in the exact direction Wei Wuxian was retreating.

Wei Wuxian was walking him backward toward the deep, cavernous trench behind the altar—straight toward that empty, lavishly lacquered coffin.

If he could coax the titan inside, Wei Wuxian had a dozen ways to seal the lid tight.

The white toxic vapor had already thinned out into harmless wisps of steam. Led by the jaunty whistle, Nie Mingjue arrived before the open coffin, his dead instincts flaring with immediate, stubborn resistance.

Wei Wuxian circled the perimeter of the pit, never breaking the tempo.

The entire hall held its breath, tracking his every shift—especially Lan Wangji, whose eyes were burned onto him.

Continuing the lighthearted trill, Wei Wuxian casually let his gaze slide across the floorboards, catching Lan Wangji’s focus. The instant their eyes met, Wei Wuxian cheekily dropped his left eyelid, throwing him an unabashed, playful wink.

It was like a thread of pure honey had slipped past his guard; beneath Lan Wangji’s steady fingers, the guqin melody rippled with a microscopic, breathless tremor before snapping instantly back to perfection.

Smug as hell, Wei Wuxian turned back to the coffin, leaning down to pat the lacquered timber with a friendly, welcoming slap.

Finally, Nie Mingjue’s iron knees bent, leaning slowly toward the open interior.

Just as his heavy torso tilted over the edge, an agonizing shriek tore through the front hall!

Nie Mingjue’s momentum halted instantly. Along with everyone else in the room, the titan whipped his head back toward the commotion.

Across the tiles, Su She was carrying a half-conscious Jin Guangyao on his back, one arm steadying the man's legs while his other hand leveled a drawn blade slick with fresh, bright blood.

A few feet away, Nie Huaisang was writhing across the floorboards, clutching his pierced thigh in screaming agony.

Before Su She could move, a concussive blast of sword glare from Shuoyue slammed down onto his wrist. Su She’s face twisted in shock as the sword was knocked spinning from his grip.

The weapon had bitten deep into Nie Huaisang’s flesh, sending a sharp, copper-rich plume of blood drifting into the damp air.

Wei Wuxian cursed violently in his head: You worthless piece of shit, ruining my play at the absolute worst possible second!

Nie Huaisang and Nie Mingjue were brothers of the same father. Sniffing out that familiar bloodline wouldn't trigger Nie Mingjue’s murderous wrath, but it would set off an overwhelming, predatory curiosity. And the second that curiosity dragged him over, he was guaranteed to catch the scent of Jin Guangyao draped over Su She’s back.

Once he butchered Jin Guangyao, that blood-soaked malice would spike out of control, rendering him completely untamable!

Sure enough, a guttural, rattling growl bubbled from deep within Nie Mingjue’s throat.

Tearing away from the coffin, his milk-white eyes locked cleanly onto the limp figure slumped across Su She's shoulders. The whistle lost its grip entirely.

Like a battering ram tearing through a gale, Nie Mingjue charged across the hall, his open palm descending like a guillotine toward Jin Guangyao’s skull!

Su She twisted his frame with desperate speed. Flicking the toe of his boot, he launched his fallen sword into the air, caught the hilt, and poured every drop of his remaining spiritual power into a vicious thrust aimed straight for Nie Mingjue’s heart.

Perhaps pushed by the sheer terror of death, the strike was shockingly fast and mercilessly brutal. The blade hummed with blinding spiritual light, brilliant and dazzling—eclipsing every elegant, textbook thrust he had ever performed in his life. Even Wei Wuxian felt an involuntary urge to applaud the sheer technical beauty of the blow.

The explosive impact forced Nie Mingjue a heavy pace back. But the moment the spiritual glow dimmed, the titan surged forward once more, reaching for Jin Guangyao with relentless, unyielding hunger.

With his left hand, Su She hurled Jin Guangyao through the air toward Lan Xichen, while his right whipped his blade up in a vicious slash aimed straight for Nie Mingjue’s throat.

Nie Mingjue’s body might have been forged of impenetrable, blade-proof iron—but the crude thread stitching his severed head to his shoulders was another story entirely!
